svg.title: init always delivers the framework through a review you can see: init routes through a review from any branch, and steps aside only when you opt out
svg.text: init always delivers the framework through a review you
Scenario: init routes through a review from any branch, and steps aside only when you opt out
The main branch already exists, and the developer is on an experiment branch
The review switched off on purpose

g.text: Given GitLab holds a project whose main branch already has a first commit
GitLab's branches page for a project that already has a first commit. The main branch is the only branch, marked
"default" and "protected", on its commit "Initial commit".
The project's random name shows as "project", and dates and commit codes are hidden, so the picture is the same on every
run.
And the developer's copy is on a local experiment branch with a commit of its own
The developer's terminal, in their copy of the project. One typed line makes a branch called spike/poc, adds a line to
the README and commits it as "wip: try an idea", then prints the history.
The history shows that commit on spike/poc, where the developer now stands (HEAD), above "Initial commit", where the
main branch and its GitLab copy origin/main still are. Commit codes show as <sha>, since they change on every run.

text.tspan: git switch -c spike/poc && echo idea >> README.md && git commit -am "wip: try an idea" && git log --oneline --all

g.text: When the developer runs the installer on the experiment branch, and it
builds the framework branch from the main branch
The developer runs the installer from spike/poc and accepts every default. This card is the
end of that run. The installer says "Preparing init-framework-devsecops from main...": it
builds its own branch from the main branch, not from spike/poc.
It pushes that branch to GitLab and opens merge request !1, "chore: initialize devsecops
framework", into the main branch, then says "Installation complete!". The line "warning:
redirecting" is git saying that GitLab took the push at the same address with ".git/" at the
end, nothing more.
Then GitLab holds a merge request into the main branch that carries only the framework
commit
The Commits tab of that merge request on GitLab. It asks to merge init-framework-devsecops into main, and it carries
exactly one commit, "chore: initialize devsecops framework".
The experiment's commit "wip: try an idea" is not in it. The counters of the Pipelines and Changes tabs are hidden: they
change with every run and every new framework file.
And GitLab lists the main branch and the framework branch, never the experiment branch
The same branches page as the first card. init-framework-devsecops now stands next to the main branch, one commit ahead
of it, with its merge request "!1".
The main branch is still on "Initial commit": nobody pushed to it. There is no spike/poc: the experiment never left the
developer's machine.
When another developer starts the installer on a new project with the review switched off
A second developer, in the copy of a new empty project, types the installer command with TASK_DEVSECOPS_INIT_DIRECT=true
in front of it, and a comment saying what it is for. That setting switches the review off: no framework branch and no
merge request.
The installer starts as usual and asks its first question, "Install the complete DevSecOps framework?". The developer
then accepts every default.
Then GitLab shows the main branch alone, with no review branch and no merge request
GitLab's branches page for that project once the installer is done. The main branch is alone, on "chore: initialize
repository", the first commit the installer makes in an empty project.
There is no init-framework-devsecops branch and no merge request badge.
And the main branch on GitLab holds only the starter README
The repository page of the main branch. The Files panel and the table list one file, README.md, and its text is the name
of the project folder, "my-project".
None of the framework files the installer wrote reached the main branch.
